title: High-Throughput SAT Sampling
problem: Traditional Boolean satisfiability (SAT) sampling algorithms operate on CNF directly and are computationally expensive, limiting throughput. Conventional approaches do not leverage GPU parallelism effectively.
motivation: SAT sampling is used in verification and testing, requiring diverse valid solutions. Current heuristic samplers have limited throughput and cannot leverage GPU acceleration.
method: Transforms SAT problems by factoring CNF representations into simplified multilevel, multi-output Boolean functions. Leverages gradient-based optimization on the circuit structure, reinterpreting SAT as supervised multi-output regression enabling differentiable, parallel bit-wise operations on tensor elements.
key_novelty: GPU-accelerated SAT sampling via gradient-based optimization on refactored Boolean circuits, enabling parallel bit-wise tensor operations for diverse solution generation.
contributions: 33.6x to 523.6x speedup over state-of-the-art heuristic samplers
primary_theme: GPU-accelerated SAT sampling via gradient-based circuit optimization
